cards.text: Grab an apron, friend, because today the crowns come off FAST. God's people are split into two kingdoms: Israel in the north and Judah in the south (1 Kings 12:16-20). In the fifteenth year of Amaziah king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Jehoash becomes king of Israel, and he reigns in Samaria forty-one years.

cards.question: Same name, different man. Jeroboam son of Nebat, the first king of the northern kingdom, led Israel into sin with golden calves (1 Kings 12:20, 28-30). What does this new King Jeroboam do about those sins?

answers.text: He doesn't turn away from them
He tears down all of them
He makes Israel repent of them

cards.text: Yep. He does evil in the sight of the LORD. And yet, PLOT TWIST: this Jeroboam wins back Israel's borders, from Lebo-hamath all the way to the Sea of the Arabah.

cards.question: The LORD had said those borders would come back, through His servant the prophet. You might know this prophet: he's the same man the LORD sent to Nineveh (Jonah 1:1-2). Who is it?

cards.text: YES, it's THAT Jonah son of Amittai (Jonah 1:1), and here we learn he's the prophet from Gath-hepher. Friend, I thought years in a junk drawer was rough, and this man spent three days and three nights inside a great fish (Jonah 1:17).
So why does the LORD do this for Israel? He sees that their suffering is very bitter, slave and free, and there's no one to help Israel.

cards.question: The LORD also had said something about Israel's future. What had He said He would not do to Israel?

answers.text: Blot out its name from under heaven
Give its land to the king of Assyria
Leave it without a single prophet

cards.question: The LORD saves Israel by the hand of Jeroboam son of Jehoash, the same king who does evil in His sight.

cards.text: Jeroboam even recovers Damascus and Hamath for Israel. Then he rests with his fathers, and his son Zechariah reigns in his place.
Down south in Judah, in Jeroboam's twenty-seventh year, Azariah son of Amaziah becomes king at SIXTEEN and reigns in Jerusalem FIFTY-TWO YEARS. Friend, my batches don't last fifty-two MINUTES.

cards.question: Azariah's father Amaziah did what was right in the eyes of the LORD (2 Kings 14:3). Like his father, Azariah does what is right too.

cards.text: He sure does. But you KNOW there's a but: the high places are not taken away.

cards.question: During Azariah's reign, what do the people keep doing at the high places?

cards.text: Then the LORD afflicts King Azariah with leprosy until the day he dies, and he lives in a separate house.

cards.question: With King Azariah sick with leprosy, who takes charge of the palace and governs the people of the land?
King Azariah rests with his fathers and is buried near them in the City of David. Then his son ___ reigns in his place.

cards.text: Back up north. In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah's reign over Judah, Jeroboam's son Zechariah becomes king of Israel in Samaria.

cards.question: Unlike his father Jeroboam, King Zechariah turns away from the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat had caused Israel to commit.

cards.text: Nope. He does evil as his fathers had done, and he reigns only six MONTHS before Shallum son of Jabesh conspires against him.

cards.question: How does Shallum's conspiracy against King Zechariah end?

answers.text: He kills Zechariah in front of the people
He drives Zechariah out of Samaria
He makes Zechariah give up the throne

cards.text: Then the passage points out that a word the LORD spoke to Jehu, an earlier king of Israel, has come true. Jehu's line on the throne went Jehu, then Jehoahaz, then Jehoash, then Jeroboam, then Zechariah (2 Kings 10:35; 13:9; 14:16, 29).

cards.question: The LORD had told Jehu that ___ generations of his sons would sit on the throne of Israel.

cards.text: Shallum becomes king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah's reign over Judah, and Uzziah is just another name for Azariah (2 Kings 15:7, 32). He reigns in Samaria one full month.
ONE MONTH. Friend, I've had dust sit on me in that junk drawer longer than this man sat on a throne. Then Menahem son of Gadi comes up from Tirzah to Samaria.

cards.question: Menahem son of Gadi strikes down and kills Shallum, and reigns in his place.
Then Menahem, starting from Tirzah, attacks the town of Tiphsah and everyone around it. Why does he attack Tiphsah?

answers.text: They would not open their gates
They had sided with the king of Judah

cards.text: No joke here, friend. The attack is brutal: Menahem rips open all the pregnant women.
Menahem reigns ten years in Samaria, and through his whole reign he doesn't turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat. Then Pul king of Assyria invades the land.

cards.question: When Pul king of Assyria invades, Menahem hands him a thousand talents of silver. What is Menahem after?

answers.text: His support to hold the kingdom
His help against the king of Aram

cards.question: A thousand talents is a LOT of silver. Who does Menahem collect it from?
Once Menahem pays the silver, the king of Assyria stays and takes over Samaria.

cards.text: Every wealthy man in Israel gets the same bill, fifty shekels of silver, and there's no number to call to dispute it. Then Menahem rests with his fathers, and his son Pekahiah reigns in his place.
In the fiftieth year of Azariah's reign over Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem becomes king of Israel. He reigns two years in Samaria, and he does evil in the sight of the LORD.

cards.question: Then one of King Pekahiah's own officers conspires against him. Who is it?

cards.text: With Argob, Arieh and fifty men of Gilead, Pekah strikes down Pekahiah at the citadel of the king's palace and reigns in his place. Pekah takes the throne from PEKAHIAH, and friend, I've read that three times and I'm STILL checking who's who.

cards.question: Pekah son of Remaliah reigns over Israel in Samaria twenty years, and he does ___ in the sight of the LORD.

cards.text: Like the kings before him, Pekah doesn't turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat. In his days, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria comes and captures a whole list of towns, plus Gilead, Galilee and all the land of Naphtali.

cards.question: Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria leaves the people he captures in their own land.
Then Hoshea son of Elah leads a conspiracy against King Pekah. What does Hoshea do?

cards.text: Down south in Judah, in the second year of Pekah's reign, Jotham son of Uzziah becomes king. He's twenty-five, and he reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem.

cards.question: How does King Jotham of Judah do in the eyes of the LORD?

answers.text: Right just like his father Uzziah
Evil just like the kings of Israel
Right at first and evil later

cards.question: Under King Jotham, the high places are finally taken away.

cards.text: Yep, the high places stay, and the people keep sacrificing and burning incense there. But Jotham does rebuild the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD.
Here the passage looks back at Jotham's days, while Pekah is still king of Israel. That's when the LORD begins to send Rezin king of Aram against Judah, and Rezin isn't coming alone.

cards.question: In Jotham's days, the LORD begins to send Rezin king of Aram against Judah. Which king of Israel does He send along with him?

cards.text: Jotham rests with his fathers and is buried with them in the City of David, and his son Ahaz reigns in his place. Friend, that is a WHOLE lot of crowns for one batch.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Blot out its name from under heaven' keeps the Bible's wording and sounds more like the Bible than the two plain modern wrong answers ('Give its land to the king of Assyria', 'Leave it without a single prophet'). The right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The earlier story cards already give this answer away. Card 3 says the evil King Jeroboam wins back Israel's borders. Card 4 says the LORD had said those borders would come back. Card 6 asks 'So why does the LORD do this for Israel?' By then the baker has been told that the LORD saves Israel through this evil king, so the true or false only restates a told fact.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The story card lists Jehu's line as Jehu, then Jehoahaz, then Jehoash, then Jeroboam, then Zechariah. Card 6 asks how many generations of Jehu's sons would sit on the throne. Counting the four sons in the list hands over 'four', and 'three' and 'seven' are ruled out.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The question asks whether Zechariah turns away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat (2 Kings 15:9). That refrain already appeared at 2 Kings 14:24 and was asked on stop 1, card 2.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: The blank asks whether Pekah does 'evil' in the sight of the LORD (2 Kings 15:28). The same line already appears at 2 Kings 14:24, 15:9, 15:18 and 15:24, and the walkthrough has already asked about it. The two wrong answers ('right', 'good') also mean the same thing, which makes 'evil' easy to pick by elimination.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: The card asks whether Jotham did right like his father (2 Kings 15:34). This repeats the line 'did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father ... had done' from 2 Kings 15:3, which was asked on stop 1, card 11.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: The card asks whether the high places are taken away under Jotham (2 Kings 15:35). The line 'Nevertheless, the high places were not taken away; the people continued sacrificing and burning incense there' repeats 2 Kings 15:4 word for word, and stop 1, cards 12 and 13 already covered it.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: 2 Kings 15:30 says Hoshea killed Pekah 'and reigned in his place.' No card ever tells the baker that Hoshea becomes king of Israel, so the baker leaves without knowing who rules Israel at the end of the passage. Card 8 moves straight to Jotham.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The setup says 'while Pekah is still king of Israel.' Card 13 then asks which king of Israel the LORD sends with Rezin, and the answer is Pekah. The setup also rules out the wrong answers: card 8 already said Jotham's reign began in Pekah's second year, so Menahem and Shallum were no longer kings in Jotham's days.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
